lessons.title: Past: 먹었어요/였어요
lessons.learn: Past power! 먹어요→먹었어요 (ate), 가요→갔어요 (went). 입니다→이었어요/였어요: 학생이었어요 (was a student). Time words: 어제 (yesterday), 오늘 (today), 내일 (tomorrow)!

grammar.title: 었/았어요 · 이었어요
grammar.explain: 먹→먹었어요, 가→갔어요, 하→했어요. 학생이었어요 (was a student), 아니었어요 (wasn't). 이미 + past = already: 이미 먹었어요!
mistakes: Saying 먹었어요 for habits — 었어요 = finished past!

lessons.title: Want: -고 싶어요
lessons.learn: Desire grammar! -고 싶어요 (I want to…): 먹고 싶어요 (want to eat), 가고 싶어요 (want to go). Requests: -아/어 주세요 (please do): 봐 주세요! Want + please = unstoppable!

grammar.title: -고 싶어요 · -아/어 주세요
grammar.explain: 먹고 싶어요 (want to eat), 자고 싶어요 (want to sleep). 보고 싶어요 ALSO means I MISS you! Requests: 도와주세요 (please help), 보여 주세요 (please show)!

examples.en: I miss you! / I want to see (you)!

mistakes: Saying 먹고 싶다 to elders — polite: 싶어요!
Saying 보고 싶어 for missing — needs 보고 싶어요!

lessons.title: 약속을 잡아요
lessons.learn: Making an appointment moves between two question shapes: -(으)ㄹ까요? invites, 어때요? asks how something suits. The future -(으)ㄹ 거예요 states what will happen once the time is agreed.

grammar.title: Proposing and agreeing
grammar.pattern: 토요일 어때요? · 몇 시에 만날까요? · 두 시에 만나요 · 좋아요
grammar.explain: 어때요? asks whether a suggestion suits; -(으)ㄹ까요? asks the other person to decide with you. The answer can be as short as 좋아요, and the agreed time takes 에: 두 시에 만나요.

mistakes.why: 어때요 is a whole question; do not put another verb in front of it.
The contrastive 은/는 marks the alternative day you are proposing.

dialogue.t: 미나 씨, 이번 주말에 시간 있어요?
dialogue.r: mina ssi, ibeon jumare sigan iss-eoyo?
dialogue.en: Mina, do you have time this weekend?
Shall we see a film? What time is good?

dialogue.t: 세 시는 어때요? 그다음에 커피도 마셔요.
dialogue.r: se si-neun eottaeyo? geudaeum-e keopido masyeoyo.
dialogue.en: How about three? And coffee afterwards.

lessons.title: Particles: 에/에서/으로
lessons.learn: Place particles! 에 (to/at-point), 에서 (action-at/from), 으로 (toward/by). 학교에 가요 (go to school), 학교에서 공부해요 (study AT school), 버스로 가요 (go BY bus)! 여기/거기/저기 = here/there/over there!

grammar.title: 에 (to) · 에서 (at) · 으로 (by)
grammar.explain: 학교에 가요 (go to school), 집에 있어요 (am at home), 학교에서 공부해요 (study at school), 버스로 가요 (go by bus)!
grammar.pattern: 에 + go · 에서 + action · 으로 + vehicle
mistakes: Saying 학교에서 가요 — going needs 에!
Saying 학교에 공부해요 — actions need 에서!

lessons.title: 가요/와요/돌아가요
lessons.learn: Move! 가요 (go), 와요 (come), 돌아가요 (return). Time + 에: 여섯 시에 (at 6). 내일 학교에 가요 = Tomorrow I go to school. Leaving: 다녀오겠습니다! Back: 다녀왔어요!

grammar.title: Movement + 시에
grammar.explain: 여섯 시에 가요 (go at 6), 내일 와요 (come tomorrow). Leaving home: 다녀오겠습니다! Return: 다녀왔어요! Family: 잘 다녀왔어요!
mistakes: Saying 여섯 시 가요 without 에 — clock-times need 에!
Saying 안녕히 가세요 when YOU leave — you say 다녀오겠습니다!

lessons.title: 지하철을 타요
lessons.learn: A journey is built from three endings: -(으)로 for the line or vehicle you take, 에서 for where you get off or change, and 까지 for the destination. 교통카드 does the paying.

grammar.title: Getting there
grammar.explain: The line you take or change to takes -(으)로; the station where you get off takes 에서; the destination takes 까지. 갈아타다 already means change, so the vehicle that follows is the one you change onto.

examples.en: I get off at Gangnam station.
How long does it take to Seoul station?

mistakes.why: The line you change to takes -(으)로, not 을/를.
A vehicle you change to takes the same -(으)로.

dialogue.en: Jihun, how do I get to Gangnam?
Transfer to line two. Do you have a transit card?
Yes. Where do I get off?

dialogue.t: 강남역에서 내리면 돼요. 십 분쯤 걸려요.
dialogue.r: gangnamyeok-eseo naerimyeon dwaeyo. sip bun-jjeum geollyeoyo.
dialogue.en: You just get off at Gangnam station. It takes about ten minutes.

lessons.title: 시장에서 값을 깎아요
lessons.learn: At a market a price is a conversation. 싸게 해 주세요 asks for a lower price, -면 makes it conditional on quantity, and the reply usually names a number and stops.

grammar.title: Asking for a price
grammar.pattern: 얼마예요? · 두 개 사면 얼마예요? · 좀 싸게 해 주세요
grammar.explain: The conditional -면 turns quantity into a bargain: 두 개 사면 얼마예요? asks what two would cost. The request 싸게 해 주세요 works on the price with 하다 — 만들다 would mean making an object, not lowering a number.

examples.en: How much if I buy two?
Make it a little cheaper, please.

mistakes.why: A price is lowered with 하다; 만들다 makes a thing.
-니까 links the reason to the request in one sentence.

dialogue.en: How much is a box of these tangerines?
Then I will give you both for twenty-eight thousand.

culture.text: A Korean meal arrives all at once. 반찬, the small side dishes, are refilled without asking at most restaurants, and the rice and soup are yours alone. Because 반찬 and 물 are shared, the polite habit is to fill a neighbour's glass before your own and to leave the last piece alone until somebody offers it. 수저 come in a rolled set, and using the spoon for rice and the chopsticks for 반찬 is the quiet default.

reading.text: 지난 주말에 미나 씨와 부산에 갔어요. 아침 일찍 기차를 타고 바다를 봤어요. 점심에는 회를 먹었는데 아주 신선했어요. 오후에는 시장에 갔습니다. 과일이 비쌌지만 커피는 싸게 샀어요. 저녁에 비가 와서 우산을 하나 사야 했어요. 그래도 좋은 여행이었습니다. 다음에는 사진을 더 많이 찍고 싶어요.
reading.gloss: Last weekend I went to Busan with Mina. We took an early train and saw the sea. For lunch we ate raw fish, and it was very fresh. In the afternoon we went to the market. The fruit was expensive, but we bought coffee cheaply. In the evening it rained, so we had to buy an umbrella. It was a good trip anyway. Next time I want to take more photographs.

listening.script:
점원: 어서 오세요. 뭐 드릴까요?
지훈: 김밥 두 줄 주세요. 그리고 물도 주세요.
점원: 네, 여기 있습니다. 만 원입니다.
지훈: 카드로 될까요?
점원: 그럼요. 포장해 드릴까요?
지훈: 아니요, 여기서 먹겠습니다.
listening.gloss: Server: Welcome, what would you like? Jihun: Two rolls of gimbap, please. And water too. Server: Here you are. That is ten thousand won. Jihun: Can I pay by card? Server: Of course. Shall I wrap it to go? Jihun: No, I will eat here.

mistakes.why: 어제 is past, so the verb carries -았/었-; the present form belongs to 오늘.
싶어요 ends the sentence — a second verb cannot follow it.
A wish is made on the stem with -고 싶어요, never on the finished form 가요.

task.instructions: Write six to eight sentences about a real or imagined outing, using at least four past-tense verbs, one -고 싶어요 wish and one price. Then rewrite two of the past sentences in the polite 합니다 form.
